answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, an economy of AI agents can employ a mechanism known as "Digital Quill Signatures". This method relies on a trusted third-party entity, akin to a digital notary, to verify the authenticity of an agent's identity. As an attacker attempts to flood the network with fake identities, the quill's verification process becomes increasingly cumbersome, reaching a nadir in efficiency. The cumulative ripple effect of this increased verification burden renders the fake identities economically unviable, effectively resisting the Sybil attack.
